utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Okay, let's get started, um, three things today - the order-tracking datastore, sprint dates, and, Tomas, your CI thing.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Yeah the CI thing can be quick. Datastore first though, that one blocks me.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: So, I've been thinking about this, and I'd say we just go with MongoDB for the order-tracking service.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Hm. Why Mongo, specifically?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Because the schema's going to keep moving for the first few months - carriers, return flows, whatever finance asks for. With documents we don't write a migration every time someone adds a field, we just ship.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I mean, that part's true, we changed the shipment object twice last quarter.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Sure, but- no, okay, go on, I don't want to derail this.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Is anyone else hungry? Sorry. Ignore me.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Ha, lunch after. Arjun, you're confident enough about the, the document model?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Yeah, for now. I can have a prototype by next week.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Fine. Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Sprint dates - I was thinking we start on the 17th, does that clash with anyone?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: I'm out on the 18th, but that's, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Okay so the CI thing - the flaky tests are mostly the payment mocks. I'll pin them this week.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Great. That's it, thanks everyone.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Quick recap on the datastore - Arjun has the Mongo prototype running, right?

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Running, yeah, it's on the staging box. Orders go in, shipment events attach as sub-documents.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: So - I ran a load test on it over the weekend, because I was curious. At about two million orders the daily report aggregation takes, I think, thirty-eight seconds, and it was still climbing.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Thirty-eight seconds? That might be the index, I didn't tune-

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: I don't think it's the index. This is what I was worried about last time. The report is basically joins across orders and payments, and finance is going to want consistent transactions across those, which is not what Mongo's great at. I think this gets worse, not better, as we grow.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: I mean, I could denormalize the payments in.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: And then you've got two copies of every payment to keep in sync.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: Can I ask a dumb question - does finance actually need the transactions?

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: They said they do. Audit thing.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Okay. I don't want to decide this on the fly. Let's all think and, um, come back to it Monday.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Other thing - the carrier demo is on the 20th, so...

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: That's tight with the sprint starting on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: I know. We'll talk about it after.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Right. So, the datastore again. Having sat with it - the load test numbers, and finance needing those transactions - I think we have to reopen the decision.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: Yeah. I've been poking at it all weekend and, honestly, the denormalizing thing is getting ugly.

utterances.speaker: Lena
utterances.text: Can I make the case for Postgres? With JSONB we still get the flexible fields Arjun wanted, so the schema thing isn't lost, and we get joins and proper transactions. And we've barely written any Mongo code, so switching now costs us maybe a week.

utterances.speaker: Wei
utterances.text: A week is fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Tomas
utterances.text: I can help with the, the migrations tooling, if that's the plan.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: I'm, yeah. I'm okay with it. It was a fair bet but the numbers don't lie.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Okay, decision: we're switching the order-tracking service to PostgreSQL. Arjun, you redo the schema this sprint, Lena reviews.

utterances.speaker: Arjun
utterances.text: On it.

utterances.speaker: Meera
utterances.text: Good. Sprint planning in five minutes, grab coffee.
